item.title: Who is Arjun Rajput? The left-handed batter who came to India's rescue against Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup
item.description: NEW DELHI: India’s Under-19 batter Arjun Rajput came to his team's rescue with a brilliant century against Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup on Sunday. The youngster from Jalandhar showed great composure when India were struggling at 22/3 after choosing to bat first at the Ministry Turf 1. Rajput walked in at No. 5, with the team desperately needing a partnership. However, Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, could score only 22 off 40 balls. Anvay Dravid, son of former India captain and coach Rahul Dravid, also failed to make a significant contribution. With wickets falling at the other end, Rajput took responsibility and played attacking cricket. He used sweeps against spinners and played aerial shots against fast bowlers to put pressure back on Pakistan. He scored 107 off 85 balls, hitting 11 fours and five sixes, before getting dismissed. His innings helped India reach 208 before being bowled out in 46.3 overs. Who is Arjun Rajput? The 18-year-old from Jalandhar, Punjab, received his first call-up to India's Under-19 team in July this year. He had an impressive run in the 2026-27 Under-19 Vinoo Mankad Trophy, where he scored 695 runs in eight innings and helped Punjab win the title. He also scored an unbeaten 55 off 33 balls in the final. Rajput had earlier made headlines playing for Ludhiana Lions in the Sher-E-Punjab T20 Cup, where he smashed 78 off just 46 balls against Mohali. Cricket runs in his passion, but his family background is a humble one. The youngster's journey to the India U-19 team has been shaped by years of hard work and family sacrifices. His father, Hoti Ram, initially earned a living by selling chhole-kulche from a roadside cart in Jalandhar. He later moved to a small bakery, from where he continues to prepare and deliver kulchas. Speaking about his son's journey, he told NDTV Sports, “I have been making kulchas for many years. Arjun has been playing cricket since the age of five years. He is very talented and hardworking.” Rajput began training at the Harbhajan Singh Cricket Academy before continuing his development under coach Vikram Sidhu. He also contributed with the ball against Nepal in India's tournament opener, taking three wickets for just eight runs.

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Ben Shelton in thrilling final for first Paris Masters title
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz ’s excellent comeback continued as he defeated Ben Shelton 7-6(5) 7-5 to claim the Paris Masters title for the first time. World No 3 Alcaraz missed nearly five months of the 2026 season with a wrist injury and his initial comeback came to an end at Shelton’s hands, with the American triumphing in a epic five-setter in the US Open quarter-finals. Since then Alcaraz has lifted ATP 500 titles in Tokyo and Vienna, the latter just last week. Despite not playing at his fluid best he scraped through in Paris - saving two match points against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals - and he continued his late-season surge with victory in an entertaining encounter between two of the tour’s flair players and his first meeting with Shelton since New York. Shelton made an assured start on serve and it was Alcaraz who came under pressure first, falling 0-40 down as the American led 2-1. But the Spaniard saved four break points to hold in a near eight-minute game, with a combination of deft volleys and aggression from the back of the court. Both players struggled to take their chances as Shelton saved two break points - one with a sublime angled volley - to keep things on serve for a 4-3 lead, then spurned another two chances to break before Alcaraz held for 4-4 with a punishing, unreturned first serve. Inevitably the first set went to a tiebreak, a contest of frequent momentum swings as eight of the 12 points went against serve. Shelton battled back from 1-3 down with an explosive smash while back-pedalling to the baseline, but could not press his advantage home. Alcaraz set up two set points with a fierce backhand volley, spurning the first thanks to an unhelpful net cord which just dipped back onto his side, but let out a roar of relief as Shelton blasted a forehand wide to concede the first set 7-6(5) in just over an hour. US Open runner-up Shelton won his previous three matches in Paris in three sets and would be forced to attempt another escape act, starting from 0-30 down in his first service game of the second set. Ben Shelton's athleticism and serve posed problems (Getty) Four big first serves helped him out of trouble and he was rewarded for his patience as he finally broke Alcaraz’s serve for a 3-2 lead, the first break of the match, with a fierce angled return that Alcaraz could only send long. A superb overhead smash from the American in the next game led to the first sign of genuine frustration for Alcaraz, who mimed throwing his racquet to the ground, as Shelton held to love. The seven-time major winner was not at his best but took advantage of a dip in concentration by Shelton to break back to 15 in his next service game, levelling things for 4-4. A superb point in the next game encapsulated the match: Shelton didn’t do a lot wrong in a finely-balanced rally until he sent a volley straight back at the Spaniard, with Alcaraz capitalising on acres of open space to plant the winner behind him, geeing up the appreciative crowd on his way

item.title: Garcia, Schick take Leverkusen to derby win at Cologne
item.description: Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin on Sunday (Silas Stein) Goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne on Sunday, lifting the visitors to fifth in the Bundesliga table. Garcia curled an excellent effort into the top corner after just seven minutes and Schick scored five minutes from time in a fiery encounter which produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the hosts. Germany starlet Said El Mala scored a stoppage-time consolation goal for the hosts, who sit in 15th spot, just one clear of the relegation playoff placing. One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart. The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated. Leverkusen broke through just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on. Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide. Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half. Schick had a goal rubbed out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league games this season. El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback. Later on Sunday, Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin, while Hoffenheim host promoted Schalke. dwi/ea

Christian Pulisic and Alphadjo Cisse provided the goals as Ruben Amorim's side climbed the Serie A table. AC Milan demonstrated tactical superiority in a dominant opening period at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, effectively deciding the contest within the first twenty minutes. Ruben Amorim’s side operated with a fluid 3-4-3 system that overwhelmed Genoa’s defensive lines, finding the breakthrough in the 13th minute when Alphadjo Cisse clinical finished following excellent work by Adrien Rabiot. The pressure remained relentless, and just six minutes later, Christian Pulisic doubled the advantage after being teed up by Goncalo Ramos, capping off a sequence of sophisticated positional play. However, the second half saw a significant shift in momentum as Milan opted for a more conservative block, allowing Genoa to grow into the game. The hosts dominated the shot count 17 to 6, eventually finding a way back through Mikael Ellertsson in the 88th minute. Despite the late tension and a yellow card for Mario Gila during the frantic closing stages, Milan’s defensive structural integrity held firm. The victory moves the Rossoneri to 24 points, keeping them firmly in the hunt for the Scudetto following a professional, if eventually nervy, performance. His distribution remained a key facet of Milan's transition play. He faced more scrutiny in the second period as Genoa pushed forward, but he contributed to the team's 15 total clearances to see out the result. item.description: Gomez's strike was his second of the season [Getty Images] Could Brighton really do the impossible and win the Premier League this season? item.description: Napoli celebrate after Lazio midfielder Alfonso Pedraza scores an own goal in the Italian Serie A football match in Naples (CARLO HERMANN) Serie A leaders Lazio dropped points for just the second time this season in Sunday's 1-1 draw away to struggling Napoli, while AC Milan climbed into the top four with a 2-1 win at Genoa. Davide Frattesi gave the Romans a deserved lead but Napoli drew level early in the second half through an Alfonso Pedraza own goal. Napoli were under pressure to deliver a result after defeats by Juventus and Porto saw the squad sent into a training retreat in a bid to revive their flagging form. But they could only claim a point against Gennaro Gattuso's unbeaten outfit, whose remarkable form continued as they moved two points clear on top on 29 points, 14 ahead of Napoli in 10th place. "We must keep going, everything's not lost even if we are behind in the standings," Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri told DAZN. "We are not out of the race for the top four, the Coppa Italia or the Champions League. There are difficult moments over the course of a season, and they must be faced calmly." The visitors, targeting a seventh league win in a row and fifth consecutive away victory in Naples, started strongly as Gustav Isaksen and Josip Sutalo drew diving saves from Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. The Romans went in front in the 28th minute when Frattesi raced on to Tijjani Noslin's through ball and finished emphatically for his fourth goal of the season. Lazio's opener sparked a reaction from Napoli as Christos Mandas denied Rasmus Hojlund before half-time substitute Pedraza inadvertently turned a cross into his own net early in the second half. The hosts came closest to a winner as Scott McTominay tested Mandas with a low shot before Kevin De Bruyne saw a shot charged down by the Greek goalkeeper and the rebound cleared off the line by Reda Belahyane. - Milan bounce back - Milan moved above Como into fourth as Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic struck in a 2-1 victory. Milan claimed a memorable derby win over rivals Inter Milan last weekend, but inconsistency reared its head again with a 2-0 Europa League loss at home to Ferencvaros on Thursday. Amorim was left furious by his side's performance in that game but saw a much improved start from his players at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris. Cisse swept in the opener after 13 minutes for his fifth league goal of the season, before Pulisic took advantage of a defensive mix-up to double their lead six minutes later. item.title: Liverpool back on track after beating Palace
item.description: Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz celebrates after scoring against Crystal Palace (Henry NICHOLLS) Florian Wirtz bagged his first Premier League goal this season as Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday. Andoni Iraola's side erased the bitter taste of successive losses to Arsenal and Fenerbahce with a comfortable victory at Selhurst Park. Alexis Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead late in the first half before Wirtz, whose last league goal came against the same opponents in April, doubled the Reds' advantage nine minutes into the second half. Alexander Isak netted Liverpool's third in the 89th minute before Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty for bottom of the table Palace. Liverpool are up to fourth place after their fourth away league win this season. It was a much-needed success for Iraola, who had started to hear some awkward questions about Liverpool's inconsistent run in his first season in charge after arriving from Bournemouth to replace the sacked Arne Slot. Yeremy Pino went agonisingly close to opening the scoring for Palace in the 18th minute when he curled against the bar. Palace striker Jorgen Strand Larsen had the ball in the back of Alisson Becker's net in the 33rd minute. But his celebrations were cut short by the offside flag and a subsequent VAR check. Mac Allister made Palace pay for those misses in the 40th minute, nodding home a Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick in clinical fashion. Wirtz increased Liverpool's advantage in the 54th minute, guiding a low Bradley Barcola cross into the bottom corner. Palace had a huge chance with just under 15 minutes remaining when Pino was denied by Alisson, who then saved from Jefferson Lerma before Nketiah lashed over. Sweden striker Isak put the result beyond doubt in the 89th minute with a deflected close-range strike. Palace earned a penalty after Dario Osorio clashed heads with Milos Kerkez but Nketiah's goal was no consolation for under-fire Eagles boss Pierre Sage. smg/dmc

item.title: Barcelona register interest in signing €80 million-rated Chelsea defender – report
item.description: Barcelona register interest in signing €80 million-rated Chelsea defender – report It is no secret that Barcelona are in dire need of reinforcements in the defensive department, having been dealt multiple injury blows in the past month or so. Signing a new central defender could be a priority for Barcelona in the upcoming January transfer window. The club have already been linked with multiple centre-backs heading into January and it appears there is a latest entrant on the list. Barcelona interested in Levi Colwill Colwill has been a regular under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Barcelona have registered interest in Chelsea defender Levi Colwill ahead of the January transfer window. A product of the Chelsea youth academy, Colwill is regarded highly in the Blues setup and has seen rapid growth in the past couple of years, especially after a loan spell at Brighton & Hove Albion. A left-footed centre-back with exceptional ball-playing qualities, Colwill has become a starter under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea this season. The Englishman’s performances have not gone unnoticed, with Barcelona among the clubs interested in his services, as they look to shore up their defensive unit. Signing Colwill will be tough All eyes on Colwill’s future. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) However, acquiring the services of Colwill won’t be a walk in the park for Barcelona. For one, the defender has a contract at Stamford Bridge until 2029, thus giving Chelsea some key leverage in negotiations. Moreover, the Blues want to extend the contract, which could further raise his current price tag of around €80 million, which itself is a challenge for Barcelona. There is hope that interest from Barça and Liverpool could sway Colwill into stalling negotiations with Chelsea, but coach Xabi Alonso has no desire to part ways with the defender. Chelsea, for their part, will not entertain any offers below their €80 million price-tag, thus making Colwill a costly target for the Catalans, at least under the current economic circumstances. Barcelona, therefore, may end up looking at other options, with the club notably being linked with a move for Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez , among others.

item.description: Brentford star forward banned for Arsenal match Igor Thiago is set to miss Brentford’s match against Arsenal later this month, after picking up a red card in their game against Brighton on Sunday. Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Igor Thiago has been a key player for Brentford in recent weeks, scoring three and assisting two in six games prior to Sunday’s trip away to Brighton & Hove Albion . But that run of form was brought to a swift end on the south coast, as the striker was shown a red card in the 23rd minute of their weekend Premier League fixture. Though the forward was initially shown a yellow card, it was upgraded to a red for violent conduct after a VAR review, with the ref highlighting that Thiago had “pushed his opponent in the face with force”. Photo by Charlie Crowhurst/Getty Images A violent conduct red card means Thiago will miss the next three games, including a home game against Everton and a trip to Old Trafford to face Manchester United . Notably from an Arsenal perspective, Brentford’s third upcoming game is at home to the Gunners, and their fourth is at home to Manchester City . Thiago will be out for Arsenal, then back to face their title rivals. Brentford will of course have a couple of games to adapt before then, but it’s a boost to Arsenal’s chances not to have to face the in-form striker. Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images Arsenal’s Max Dowman is serving a three-match suspension of his own, having picked up a red card in the team’s League Cup match against Fleetwood Town . item.title: ‘College GameDay’ taking surprise trip to Idaho for Oregon State-Boise State
item.description: Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images ESPN went off the board with its pick for next Saturday’s College GameDay location. The network will take its flagship college football pregame show to Boise, Idaho for a Pac-12 game between Oregon State and Boise State. The Broncos are currently in pole position to secure the automatic Group of Six spot in this year’s College Football Playoff. GET READY BOISE, WE’RE COMING TO YOUR CITY We’re heading west for a Pac-12 showdown that could have CFP implications between Oregon State and Boise State https://t.co/o9XzuwoKyv — College GameDay (@CollegeGameDay) November 8, 2026 The trip will mark the first time GameDay has traveled to a Group of Six campus since 2023 when the show went to Harrisonburg, Virginia for a game between Appalachian State and James Madison. Boise State advanced to 8-1 on Saturday after a blowout win over Colorado State; the Broncos’ lone loss this season came in their first game of the year against Oregon. Oregon State, meanwhile, sports a middling 5-4 record but is the toughest remaining game on Boise State’s schedule. Some of Saturday’s other results likely pushed the trip to Boise over the top for ESPN. Kentucky’s lopsided loss to Tennessee alongside Florida’s loss the Oklahoma made next weekend’s Florida-Kentucky matchup much less attractive. Likewise, LSU’s loss to Alabama made a return trip to Baton Rouge, where GameDay opened the season, less desirable for Texas-LSU next Saturday. Missouri-Georgia offered another sensible option for the show, but the Tigers’ loss to Texas on Saturday likely knocked Mizzou firmly out of the playoff picture. Other viable options included Utah visiting Arizona, though maybe there’s still some Pat McAfee-related considerations for avoiding the Utes even after their big win against BYU on Saturday, and USC traveling to Indiana, though GameDay was just in Bloomington last weekend. Perhaps the only other possibility would’ve been Wake Forest-SMU. The Demon Deacons are 8-1 with their lone loss coming to Miami, while SMU is still firmly in the running for an ACC title at 7-2. But given Saturday’s results, the choice was pretty wide open for GameDay ; there was no clear-cut destination for the show to go. Those are the weeks when ESPN can make the refreshing decision to show teams outside the Power-2 some love, and the network chose to do exactly that.
